mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport of each natural person UBO/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Register Extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce and Companies of the foreign jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for the designated incorporator or representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate/reference letter verifying identity and source of funds
Proof of residential address (recent utility bill) of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local utility provider or government authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Luxembourg national sanctions register prior to incorporation and at each banking relationship. PEP screening is required for all UBOs, shareholders and directors. High-risk PEPs require enhanced due diligence with source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification. Suspicious transaction reporting to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) is compulsory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in French, German, Luxembourgish, or in any other language using the Latin alphabet. Names in non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Arabic, etc.) must be transliterated or accompanied by a certified translation into French/German. The RCS requires a clear, unambiguous spelling and a distinct appellation that is not misleading.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal to the RCS within 15 days of notification, specifying the legal grounds and alternative names. If ministerial non-objection is required, the applicant may submit a formal request to the Ministry of Justice or the Ministry of the Economy. Further judicial recourse is available before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d’arrondissement) within three months of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are not accepted as a substitute for a Luxembourg registered office. A licensed domiciliation company may provide the registered address, but the SARL must maintain genuine management and operational substance in Luxembourg, including staff and premises commensurate with its VPN/SaaS business. A purely virtual or façade setup will fail commercial substance assessment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% probability of unannounced physical inspection in the first 24 months, rising to 30% under substance audits or AML-related inspections if the company is connected to a regulated financial group.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 710-1 to 710-24 (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to professions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg City; electronic filing via www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) with annexed articles of association (statuts), filed electronically with the RCS by the notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum fully subscribed and paid-up share capital of EUR 12,000 for an SARL; the capital must be deposited before notarization in a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) at a Luxembourg credit institution and is released to the company only upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.À R.L. — The undersigned sole manager (the Gérant), acting as the board of the company, hereby resolves: (1) that the share capital of EUR 12,000 has been fully subscribed and paid up by the sole shareholder, subject to the blocked-account release upon RCS registration; (2) that the registered office of the company is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) that [Name], domiciled at [address], is appointed as Gérant (manager) with sole signature authority for the company; and (4) that the Gérant is authorized to open bank accounts and complete the RCS and VAT registrations. This resolution is effective retroactively to the date of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of minimum share capital in a blocked escrow bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) chosen by the founding shareholder, e.g. BNP Paribas Luxembourg, Spuerkeess or another EEA-licensed bank with a Luxembourg branch.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the bank to open a temporary blocked account (compte bloqué) in the name of the future SARL or of the founding shareholder for the benefit of the company. Transfer at least EUR 12,000 and obtain a bank certificate of capital blockage (attestation de blocage) confirming that the funds are held until the RCS registration, with payment instructions to release the funds to the company once the registration number is granted. Deliver the certificate to the notary together with a copy of the planned subscription declarations.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID of the sole shareholder
Proof of residential address of the shareholder (recent utility bill or bank statement)
Bank account opening form for the blocked account
Reference letter from the Luxembourg notary confirming the corporate object
Draft articles of association for bank KYC review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC or source-of-funds evidence, provide certified passport pages, bank reference letters, and a sworn source-of-wealth statement; ask the notary to issue a formal instruction letter to the bank to expedite opening. If the bank refuses opening, switch to another EEA-licensed credit institution and re-submit the same documentation package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the deed of incorporation and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notaire) — chosen by the founding shareholder.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft articles of association to the notary for legal review. The notary verifies the legality of the corporate name (checking RCS name availability), the corporate object (VPN network and privacy software development, IT security consulting and SaaS services), the share capital subscription, the registered office address, and the identity of the shareholder and the first manager. On approval, the shareholder executes the deed of incorporation before the notary; the notary authenticates the deed and annexes the articles of association and the bank certificate of the blocked capital.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of the founding shareholder
Proof of address of the shareholder
Draft articles of association
Bank certificate of blocked capital (attestation de blocage)
Clean criminal record certificate (casier judiciaire) of the intended manager in Luxembourg or in the country of residence
Power of attorney if the shareholder is represented before the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary reports a name conflict with an existing registered company, submit three alternative names for a new availability check. If a clause is found non-complying with mandatory law (e.g., capital distribution rules), amend the drafts immediately and execute a rectification sheet before signing; no additional notary fee is charged if modifications are made in a single meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration of the company with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), managed by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); electronic filing via the notification to the RCS by the notary through the LBR e-platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one business day after notarization, the notary files the deed of incorporation, the articles, the bank capital certificate, the manager's consent, and the RCS filing form electronically. The RCS verifies formal legality and registers the company in the trade register, issuing the national identification number (matricule) and the registration certificate. Third-party effectiveness of the incorporation commences only upon this registration.
required_dossiers: Authentic notarial deed of incorporation
Annexed articles of association
Bank attestation of blocked capital
Statement of acceptance by the manager (consent to act)
Completed RCS registration form (signed by the notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for additional information or a refusal, the notary resubmits a corrected dossier within 8 days. In case of rejection that cannot be cured informally, appeal is available to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 15 days of the refusal notice, and a court order may compel registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation instrument in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), published by the RCS under the authority of the Ministry of Justice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the RCS automatically publishes a summary of the incorporation deed, the statutes, and the appointed officers in the RESA electronic compendium. The company receives the official publication reference and an extract of the registered statutes. This publication completes the statutory advertising requirement (publicité légale) and makes the incorporation opposable to third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extrait du registre)
Notarial deed transmitted by the notary for publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is delayed or contains errors, the notary files an acte rectificatif (corrective deed) within 15 days; for material errors affecting third parties, an application to the RCS for index correction is made under Article 24 of the 2002 Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (Direction générale des PME), Luxembourg; online portal guichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic application on guichet.lu for a simple business establishment permit covering the corporate object of software development and digital services. The applicant manager must demonstrate reliable moral standing (clean criminal record) and the required professional competence, satisfied by a university degree in IT, computer science, or by at least three years of effective management experience in the sector. The permit is company-specific and must be displayed at the registered office.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (matricule)
Extrait du casier judiciaire of the manager
Degree diploma or proof of three years of professional management experience in IT services
Identity document of the manager
Completed guichet.lu application form
Articles of association reflecting the authorized activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ministry requests additional documents (demande de complément), submit within the given deadline (generally one month) to avoid a deemed refusal. If the permit is refused, file an administrative appeal (recours) with the Tribunal administratif within one month of notification, and, in parallel, request a re-examination by the Minister of the Economy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for corporate income tax, VAT and social security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) for employer registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the manager applies for a corporate income tax file number (numéro de dossier) via the ACD using the RCS matricule, files the VAT registration form (formulaire 640) with the AEDT within 15 days of the start of economic activity, and registers as an employer with the CCSS if personnel will be hired. All filings may be completed online using MyGuichet.lu with the company's business identification number.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Notarized articles of association
Identity document and address of the manager
Bank account details (RIB) of the company
Declaration of the first financial year closing date
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT contests the VAT effective date, submit the commercial invoice or contract evidencing the actual start of operations; late registration penalties are assessed under Article 56 of the VAT law and may be appealed before the directeur de l'administration within three months. The CCSS registration is immediate once the matricule is submitted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — VPN and digital encryption software is a non-industrial service activity; the competent bodies are the Ministry of the Economy (Direction générale des PME) for the establishment permit and the RCS for corporate supervision; the ITM (Inspection du travail et des mines) supervises occupational health at office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required for a digital SaaS activity; the general autorisation d'établissement is the sole operational authorization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical production installation; the activity of software development and VPN services is not listed in Annexes I to IV of the Luxembourg Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment, and no EIA report or environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero industrial discharge, wastewater, VOC, or waste streams are generated by the digital activity; the registered office must merely comply with general municipal waste collection rules and, if office equipment is later decommissioned, the WEEE obligations under EU Directive 2012/19/EU as transposed by Luxembourg legislation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defense certification is triggered for a standard office tenancy without public access. The employer must comply with the general occupational health and safety duties enforced by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM), including a workplace risk assessment, fire safety measures (accessible extinguishers, escape routes) and, if staff are hired, a declaration to the CCSS; fire service approval is required only if the premises belong to the class of établissements recevant du public (ERP) or exceed specified floor areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxation and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT; unified company and tax registration portal: guichet.lu / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the Single Registration Desk (RBE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) must first complete company incorporation with the Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), obtaining the Luxembourg national identification number (matricule d'identification). VAT registration is then mandatory for taxable economic activities; the foreign or newly resident entity files the VAT registration application electronically via the guichet.lu business portal, with the AED issuing a Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro de TVA LU). Non-established foreign entities that make taxable supplies in Luxembourg without a fixed establishment must register directly for VAT and may be required to appoint an approved VAT representative in Luxembourg; there is no de minimis VAT registration threshold for non-established suppliers. The same matricule is used as the national tax identification number, and the VAT number must be quoted on all invoices and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box system. A SARL is classified as a fully taxable resident corporate entity from the moment of incorporation, subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune). Available statutory elections relevant to taxation include the election to form a VAT group (assujetti unique) under Article 56bis of the VAT law, and the option to enter the Luxembourg corporate tax consolidation regime for resident group members with at least 95% ownership, allowing income and expense aggregation for CIT purposes. No fiscal transparency election is available for a SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the Luxembourg small-business VAT exemption for domestic established businesses; EUR 10,000 Union-wide distance-sales threshold for B2C electronic and VPN/privacy services supplied to EU customers via the One Stop Shop (OSS); zero registration threshold for non-established foreign businesses making taxable supplies in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently has no general real-time continuous transaction control, fiscal clearance, or mandatory digital stamping regime for B2B or B2C VAT invoices. Mandatory electronic invoicing applies only for the public procurement (B2G) context through the PEPPOL network. There is no API-based pre-clearance requirement for issuing invoices; however, all invoices must satisfy Articles 56-59 of the Luxembourg VAT law, including integrity-of-content and authenticity requirements, and standardised invoice fields with the LU-VAT number and seller identification. Future EU-wide e-invoicing and e-reporting standards based on the VAT in the Digital Age package will progressively replace current rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: zero-rating on exports to non-EU destinations applies when the supplier exports the goods itself, exports them on behalf of the non-resident customer, or otherwise proves that the goods have physically left the EU within the legally required time limits, accompanied by a valid customs export declaration. For services: VPN, encryption software, and related digital/network services supplied to a non-EU business customer fall outside Luxembourg VAT under the general B2B place-of-supply rule unless the effective use and enjoyment is located in Luxembourg; services supplied to non-EU non-taxable persons are outside Luxembourg VAT when the customer is resident outside the EU and the effective use is outside the EU. VPN privacy services supplied to EU private consumers remain taxable in Luxembourg or via OSS/e-commerce simplification, excluding 0% zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Electronic Export / Export Accompanying Document lodged through Luxembourg Customs / EU Single Window)
Bill of Lading or equivalent multimodal transport document evidencing delivery to the non-EU destination
Inward remittance certificate / bank payment confirmation establishing receipt of the foreign sales consideration
Commercial invoice, proforma invoice, packing list, and proof of transport (CMR, sea waybill, airway bill or port receipts)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to intensive documentary audit by the Luxembourg VAT administration. If the supporting export evidence is incomplete, inconsistent, or fraudulent, the AED will recharacterise the supply as locally taxable at 17% VAT and issue an assessment for the tax due, plus default interest of 0.8% per month or part thereof for late/VAT withheld amounts, and administrative fines ranging from approximately 10% to 100% of the underpaid tax depending on good faith, negligence, or intentional concealment. Criminal penalties may be imposed for VAT fraud, including imprisonment and fines under Luxembourg fiscal criminal law, and the limitation period for reassessment is extended to 10 years in cases of fraud. Export zero-rating refunds may be clawed back with retrospective effect, including rejection of exporters' refund claims and inclusion of the taxpayer's name in customs risk-targeting databases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting within the Eurosystem and in conjunction with the European Central Bank
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Luxembourg franc has been superseded by the euro; Luxembourg, as a member of the euro area, imposes no foreign exchange controls on either current account or capital account transactions. Capital movements, dividend distributions, loan repayments, and liquidation proceeds are freely convertible and remittable, subject to EU anti-money laundering, sanctions, and tax compliance obligations. Profit remittance is legally unrestricted, but a 15% domestic withholding tax applies to dividends unless reduced pursuant to the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0% under qualifying conditions), a bilateral double tax treaty, or the Luxembourg tax exemption regime. The Luxembourg tax administration may require evidence of economic substance, beneficial ownership declarations, and compliance with anti-abuse rules (e.g., GAAR) before treaty benefits or withholding tax relief are granted. Practical hurdles are mainly documentary, not regulatory, including the need to file annual accounts with the Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés and to maintain appropriate substance for a société à responsabilité limitée (SARL).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender requirements in Luxembourg or the euro area. Export receipts, including revenues from VPN subscription licences, technical support services, and software royalties, may be fully retained in any currency, held on EUR or foreign-currency accounts, and freely used for working capital or investment. No mandatory conversion ratio or repatriation timeline exists. For balance-of-payments statistical reporting, resident companies must report cross-border transactions above applicable thresholds to the Banque centrale du Luxembourg on a quarterly or annual basis, but such reporting is purely statistical and does not restrict currency conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore non-EEA electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not legally recognised as credit institutions for general corporate banking purposes in Luxembourg; they cannot open a domestic payment account with a Luxembourg IBAN unless licensed under the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2) or operating through an EEA-licensed partner. EEA-licensed fintech and EMI platforms can passport their services into Luxembourg and may provide multi-currency virtual IBANs, payment processing, and FX conversion; however, corporate treasury operations, capital escrow arrangements, and material liquidity buffers are better held at a Luxembourg-authorised bank. Feasibility rating: Medium for EEA-regulated EMIs when used as auxiliary disbursement rails, but Low for offshore non-EEA EMIs as a primary treasury solution due to regulatory non-recognition, correspondent banking risk, and AML scrutiny.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg credit institutions apply a strict KYC and AML onboarding protocol under CSSF rules and the Law of 12 November 2004. In practice, for a newly established SARL, at least one director or senior manager and every ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with a controlling or senior-management role must either attend a physical onboarding interview at the bank in Luxembourg or undergo a biometric identity verification with a Luxembourg notary, a CSSF-approved agent, or the bank's own remote KYC platform where the bank expressly authorises a digital solution. Full remote opening without any physical presence is rare, particularly for medium-risk enhanced-scrutiny sectors such as VPN, privacy software, and digital encryption products. The bank mandates submission of original or certified corporate documents, and may require a confirmation meeting at a registered Luxembourg office address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anonymity-enhanced payment flows and cryptocurrency denomination of subscription fees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction monitoring controls, an anti-money laundering policy covering crypto-asset red flags, complete list of accepted payment processors (e.g., Stripe, Paymentwall), copy of the merchant agreements, risk assessment showing no crypto-outset or mixing activities, and user onboarding logs proving source-of-funds verification for any large B2B payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty or customer base in jurisdictions with weak AML standards
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-by-country customer penetration analysis, IP-geolocation evidence, export-control classification for encryption software, acceptable-use policy prohibiting sanctioned jurisdictions, sanctions screening results (EU, UN, OFAC), and a contractual clause requiring resellers and distributors to comply with EU restrictive measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between VPN subscription business model and cross-border wire transfer patterns (high-frequency, small-value, globally dispersed)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SaaS revenue recognition policy, auditable payment processor reports showing transaction routing and interbank settlement, evidence of subscription billing cycles, and a Treasury policy segregating client monies from operating funds, including a transaction-limit matrix and automated reconciliation workflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque shareholding structure, including non-resident owners or nominee arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO register underlying the SARL (including the 25% and 10% beneficial ownership thresholds), notarised articles of association, Luxembourg business register extract with PNR number, signed corporate resolutions appointing signatories, sworn declarations of non-nominee status, and audited or certified source-of-funds documentation for any capital contribution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the Luxembourg SARL should be routed via SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (EUR, within EEA) or SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments in USD or GBP. The remittance instruction must specify the payment purpose using the EU Balance of Payments coding convention: for equity capital, the purpose code 'E' (Direct Investment – Equity) or the IMF BPM6 code 'Direct Investment' is appropriate, accompanied by a shareholder resolution and subscription agreement. Luxembourg banks require verification of the source of funds through bank statements, tax returns, or audited financial statements of the contributing shareholder. The corporate bank must be notified under KYC procedures before the transfer; copies of the signed board minutes approving the capital increase, the notarised deed if a SARL statutory capital change necessitates it, and the registration filing with the Luxembourg Register de Commerce et des Sociétés must be provided. For inbound investment in the form of a shareholder loan, a written loan agreement and a detailed purpose code for 'Other Investment – Loans' must be submitted. Direct investment capital flows are freely permitted, but Luxembourg banks may request an economic substance declaration confirming the SARL's administrative and operational presence in Luxembourg.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound trade and vendor payments is the SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated disbursements to EEA beneficiaries, with SWIFT MT103 used for non-EUR and non-EEA transactions. For larger SaaS infrastructure purchases or hardware-related licensing, a commercial letter of credit (LC) may be used if the supplier requires documentary collection, but Luxembourg commercial practice for IT services is generally via irrevocable telegraphic transfer. All outbound payments must be supported by an underlying commercial invoice, contract, purchase order, or service agreement; the bank will apply sanctions screening and AML transaction monitoring. For recurring disbursements to cloud providers, data centre operators, and international bandwidth carriers, standing instructions with predetermined thresholds and sub-authorisation rules can be established. Settlement should be denominated in the same currency as the bank account to avoid unnecessary conversion; any FX conversion should be pre-agreed with the corporate treasury in accordance with the FX hedging policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable forward contracts (e.g., EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) with maturities up to 12 months
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or non-convertible currencies (e.g., USD/CNY, USD/INR) to hedge emerging-market client receipts
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and currency swaps) for medium-term hedging of the SARL's foreign-currency capex or intercompany loan exposures
European-style FX options (over-the-counter) purchased from an authorised Luxembourg credit institution to hedge adverse currency movements without downside exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur les sociétés, Form 4)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the year following the tax year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, due 31 May; extensions may be granted on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of €750–€3,750; default assessment by the tax authorities; late payment interest at 0.6% per month; criminal fines up to €50,000 for wilful omissions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net Wealth Tax Return (Imposition sur la fortune, Form 5)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the year following the tax year; concurrent with the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Minimum net wealth tax of €535 is payable annually; late payment interest at 0.6% per month; enforcement and administrative fines for non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Comptes Annuels) and Publication in the RES
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via eJustice / Recueil électronique des sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the balance sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, due 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty forced filing by the public prosecutor; administrative fine up to €5,000; reputational risk and potential strike-off after repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) Approval of Annual Accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting (internal corporate record; minutes to be held on file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened within 6 months of the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold AGM does not directly trigger a fine, but prevents valid approval of annual accounts and may be challenged by shareholders or the public prosecutor

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit required if two of the three following thresholds are exceeded consecutively for two financial years: total balance sheet > €4.4 million; net turnover > €8.8 million; average number of employees > 50. Companies not exceeding these thresholds are exempt from the annual statutory audit (révision légale).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the Law of 19 December 2002 (transposing the EU Accounting Directive); IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts and optionally for statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation filing is required in Luxembourg. Beneficial-owner data held in the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) must be updated within 30 days of any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership, and a declaration must be filed upon incorporation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $864 – $2,700 per year (typical Luxembourg registered office and corporate administration service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,400 – $16,200 per year (typical certified audit fee for a Luxembourg SARL of comparable size)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate effective rate for Luxembourg City (FY2024), composed of corporate income tax (IRC) at 15% on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable income and 17% above EUR 175,000, plus a 7% solidarity surcharge on the IRC, plus municipal business tax (ICC) at the Luxembourg City rate of 6.75%. The aggregate marginal rate is projected at 25.28% for FY2025 when the solidarity surcharge rises to 9%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No across-the-board statutory tax holiday. Available reliefs: (i) R&D tax credit of 44% of eligible research and development expenses up to EUR 450,000 and 35% above that amount (capped), applicable to software development and encryption R&D; (ii) investment tax credit (crédit d'impôt pour investissements) of up to 8% of eligible investments in tangible and certain intangible assets; (iii) participation exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains where the SARL holds at least 10% of a subsidiary's share capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period; (iv) the former 80% IP income exemption remains grandfathered only for IP acquired or developed before 30 June 2021, so newly developed VPN/encryption IP created in FY2025 is fully taxable at ordinary rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited — Luxembourg law permits indefinite carryforward of tax losses without a statutory time cap; carryback is not permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, including integrated schedules for municipal business tax and net wealth tax). Filing is mandatory in electronic format through the secure national portal MyGuichet.lu (eCDF/eTVA electronic filing module) or via a registered tax professional (comptable agréé).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, based on the calendar or financial year; four mandatory quarterly advance payments of estimated corporate income tax and municipal business tax are required in the course of the tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed by 31 May of the year following the tax year. Automatic extension to 31 December is granted where the return is filed electronically by an approved tax adviser; a further reasoned postponement may be requested from the Administration des contributions directes (ACD).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, Luxembourg tax matricule, RCS number, registered office, legal form (SARL), NACE/ISIC code 6201.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Luxembourg tax matricule and resident agent details; declare the ultimate non-resident beneficial owners; no foreign trade registry number is accepted in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period and reporting currency: opening and closing dates of the financial year; all figures in EUR.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must be reported separately in the annex as the tax administration requires individual allocation of distributed profits for withholding tax reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit and loss: turnover from VPN subscriptions, privacy software licenses, and related network services; deduction of operating costs, staffing, cloud hosting, payment processor fees (Stripe, Paymentwall), licensing, and R&D costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report revenues net of Luxembourg VAT; if the SARL functions as a commissionaire or royalty collector for non-resident principals, disclose the agency relationship and the corresponding arm's length margin in the TP annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments to commercial result: add-back of non-deductible expenses, including disallowed interest under the ATAD interest limitation rule (net interest expense exceeding 30% of EBITDA), and concealed profit distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest or royalties paid to non-resident related parties must be validated against the substance and arm's length requirements; excessive payments may be recharacterized as constructive dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption schedule: exemption claims for qualifying dividend income and capital gains from subsidiaries held at least 10% for at least 12 months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach documentary proof of the holding percentage and holding period; non-resident parent companies claiming the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefit must provide a valid certificate of tax residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss computation and carryforward schedule: unlimited carryforward of prior-year losses, with a reconciliation of the loss history.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses incurred by a foreign permanent establishment may not be used in Luxembourg unless the PE is expressly covered by a treaty loss-relief clause; include a PE loss adjustment worksheet.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax (ICC) schedules: allocation of business income to the municipal tax base by commune; Luxembourg City applies a multiplier of 3.6 on the federal base rate of 1.875%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercommunal income apportionment applies if the SARL has a permanent establishment in another commune; non-resident persons with a Luxembourg PE must file in the commune of the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax (IFT) schedule: net taxable assets as at 1 January; ordinary rate 0.5% on assets exceeding EUR 500,000; small and medium enterprises may benefit from a reduction for the first EUR 10,000,000 of taxable assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A shareholding of at least 10% in a Luxembourg company may still be taxable in Luxembourg for non-resident shareholders only under specific circumstances; the SARL must disclose asset ownership to verify the IFT filing obligation of the shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend and withholding tax reconciliation: detail of gross distributions made during the year, applicable withholding tax rate, and proof of exemption claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Standard WHT is 15%; statistical reduction to 0% or 5% requires an approved DTA/Parent-Subsidiary Directive claim, the shareholder's certificate of residence (TRC), and confirmation of the 12-month holding period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing declaration: report intercompany transactions with related parties, applied arm's length method, and functional analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident parents of the Luxembourg SARL, provide a Local File whenever controlled transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 in annual net turnover and a Master File when the group's consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and incentives: R&D credit, investment credit, and any deductible notional interest or transitional IP relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The R&D credit is available to Luxembourg resident companies that carry out qualifying R&D in Luxembourg or in the EEA; foreign contract research must be supported by a qualifying R&D agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation summary: final corporate income tax, solidarity surcharge, municipal tax, credits, net tax payable, and reconciliation with the quarterly advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any underpayment compared with the advance payments is subject to monthly late-payment interest at 0.8% from the statutory payment date; the return must be signed by a manager empowered to bind the SARL.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty of up to 10% of the assessed tax (minimum EUR 50, maximum EUR 1,000); moratory interest on late tax at 0.8% per month from the statutory due date; additional enhancement of 10% where payment is not made after formal demand; late or missing CbCR documentation: fine up to EUR 250,000; fraudulent declarations attract criminal sanctions described in the red flags section.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on distributions made by a SARL to its shareholders. The rate is reduced to 0% for qualified corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (minimum 10% shareholding held for at least 12 months) and to 5% or 15% under applicable double taxation agreements where the shareholder is the beneficial owner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief at source is granted only after the paying SARL has received the shareholder's certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the competent foreign tax authority, together with a beneficial-ownership declaration and the DTA relief form. Where relief is not granted at source, the shareholder may file a refund claim with the Administration des contributions directes within five years from the date the dividend was paid. The Luxembourg paying entity must retain the TRC and supporting documentation in its tax file and report the reduced-rate distribution in its annual return; the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI applies to deny treaty benefits where the shareholder arrangement lacks substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on outbound royalties is 0% (Luxembourg does not impose WHT on royalty payments). Outbound interest is also taxed at 0% as a general rule, with the exception of interest paid in the context of export-financing transactions subject to a 15% rate (rarely applicable). The EU Interest and Royalties Directive is therefore generally not required to reduce Luxembourg tax to zero for related-party payments. Notwithstanding the zero rates, excessive or abusive royalty and interest payments remain subject to recharacterization as constructive dividends under the arm's length and abuse-of-law rules, which would trigger the 15% dividend WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where the Luxembourg SARL's annual net turnover exceeds EUR 1,000,000 and the entity engages in controlled cross-border transactions with related enterprises. Master File: mandatory where the consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 50,000,000. Country-by-Country Report: mandatory where the ultimate parent group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds EUR 750,000,000. Electronic CbCR filing is made through the ACD's dedicated e-filing channel; documentation must be produced within 30 days upon request.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) — appropriate for licensing of VPN software and recurring subscription fees when comparable public prices exist
Resale Price Method (RPM) — appropriate for distribution and resale functions of the SARL within the group
Cost Plus Method (CPLM) — appropriate for contract development of encryption modules and service functions
Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) — the most frequently accepted method for low-risk controlled distribution, support, or development functions in Luxembourg practice
Profit Split Method (PSM) — appropriate for integrated value chains where both parties contribute unique intangible assets, including jointly developed IP for VPN and privacy applications
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but substantive economic activity is enforced through: (i) the codified general anti-abuse rule (article 6 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law, as applied through the abuse-of-law doctrine); (ii) the requirement of genuine management and real activities to establish Luxembourg tax residence and to access treaty benefits (including the MLI Principal Purpose Test); (iii) ATAD implementation, namely the 30% EBITDA interest limitation rule, CFC rules, anti-hybrid rules, and exit taxation; and (iv) administrative practice requiring substance for APA applications, transfer pricing adjustments, and the benefit of tax incentives. A SARL operating a VPN/privacy software business must demonstrably perform strategic management, contracting, staff supervision, and R&D decisions in Luxembourg, maintain an active bank account, hold periodic board meetings with actual participation, and employ adequate qualified personnel, otherwise it is exposed to recharacterization as a shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission or misrepresentation in Form 500, underreporting of VPN subscription revenues, inflation of deductible expenses through fictitious invoices, concealment of foreign bank accounts or digital-asset holdings, and deliberate destruction of accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ordinary tax fraud under Article 176 LIR: fine of EUR 10,000 to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years. Aggravated tax fraud involving cross-border artificial arrangements or a tax loss exceeding EUR 25,000: imprisonment from 1 to 10 years and fine up to EUR 250,000, in addition to reassessments, a 10% penalty, monthly interest at 0.8%, and possible publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers (gérants) and directors who knowingly sign or cause the filing of false declarations are criminally liable and may be subject to joint and several civil liability for the tax deficit under the action en comblement du passif; in serious cross-border cases, travel bans, provisional arrest, and enforcement against personal assets are available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intragroup royalty or subscription fees for VPN/encryption IP below or above arm's length; locating valuable IP in a no-tax subsidiary without substantive development; failure to prepare a Local File or Master File after the turnover thresholds are exceeded; failure to produce documentation within 30 days of a formal request; absence of a functional analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment to the arm's length result, with a penalty surcharge of 10% on the additional assessment; late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; failure to file a valid CbCR or documentation can attract fines up to EUR 250,000; artificially structured mispricing may be recharacterized as a constructive dividend subject to 15% withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the incremental tax and penalties where they caused or tolerated the incorrect transfer pricing policy without professional advice; criminal liability arises if the documentation is deliberately falsified; civil seizure of personal property is possible where the company is insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Luxembourg registered office with no staff, no local management, no operating bank account, and no business activity; using nominee directors; routing VPN service revenues through Luxembourg solely to access treaty or EU directives benefits while all decisions and functions occur abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of Luxembourg tax residence, recharacterization under the GAAR, application or denial of treaty relief under the Principal Purpose Test, reassessment of profits with 0.8% monthly interest and a 10% penalty; possible loss of the net wealth tax SME exemption and exposure to full 0.5% net wealth tax; the Luxembourg authorities may also strike the company from the RCS for non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners risk personal liability for the company's unpaid taxes where the corporate form is used as a fraudulent device; criminal sanctions for falsification of financial statements, travel restrictions, and prohibition from managing companies in Luxembourg may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Constructive Dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to shareholders without collecting the 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; baselessly applying the 0% EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive rate where the holding period or threshold is not met; failing to obtain a TRC; disguising distributions as excess management fees, loans, or royalty payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full 15% withholding tax on the payer SARL, plus a 10% penalty and monthly late interest; where the foreign shareholder lacks treaty substance, the treaty relief is rejected and the standard 15% WHT is recovered from the distributing company; penalties for failure to withhold are assessed directly on the directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The manager who makes a distribution without collecting the WHT becomes personally liable to the tax authorities for the full withheld amount; criminal fines of EUR 1,000 to EUR 5,000 apply to recalcitrant officers; in fraud cases, imprisonment and travel bans are possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the VPN/privacy app with anonymous payment acceptance, absence of transaction monitoring, use of Stripe and Paymentwall without KYC screening of resellers, processing payments for sanctioned entities, enabling cryptocurrency payments without registration as a virtual asset service provider, or concealing the economic beneficiary of the revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 as amended and CSSF Regulation 12-02 impose administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; if the SARL is deemed to engage in crypto-asset services without authorization, cease-and-desist orders and sanctioning of the payment service providers follow; freezes of funds and termination of processing agreements by Stripe and Paymentwall are typical operational consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted under Articles 506-1 to 506-8 of the Luxembourg Criminal Code for money laundering, with imprisonment up to 5 years and criminal fines up to EUR 1,250,000; civil seizure, travel bans, and prohibition on exercising commercial functions apply; supervisors and compliance officers are individually liable for the absence of effective AML controls.
